payload.description:
**Follow-on to PPY-8f5273** under `PPY-54055d`.

Steal the **gate design** from Chattic.us-web `publication-writing` (`rules.yml` + rejected/published corpus). Do **not** move the Chatticus website onto Papyrus hosting. That CMS question is later and separate.

## Intent

As a publication operator, I want diagnose to load banned phrases, intensifiers, and patterns from the style profile and to regress against both house-voice excerpts that must pass and brochure slop that must fail, so new rules are added from misses instead of hardcoded Python.

## Why (Chatticus lessons we are taking)

- Voice prose (`style-profile.yml` tone/audience/samples) stays the source of truth for writers. The **deterministic subset** is data, updated when policy changes.
- Grow rules from a **two-sided corpus**: a rejected draft that is not caught is a missing rule; a rule that flags a published house-voice excerpt is too aggressive.
- Only automate what a script can decide (word lists, regex patterns, contrast counts). Do not regex “does this say what changed for the reader.”
- Diagnose stays **advisory** JSON. Chatticus’s fail-closed exit is a site CI gate, not this loop.

## Done when

- Style profile may include an optional `rules:` mapping:
  - `bannedPhrases` (list of strings)
  - `bannedIntensifiers` (list of strings, word-boundary match)
  - `bannedPatterns` (list of `{pattern, message}`)
  - `contrastCap` (integer, or `null` / omitted to disable)
- Omitting `rules:` does not break existing profiles; heuristic checks from PPY-156189 / PPY-8f5273 still run subject to `checks:`.
- Diagnose emits findings from those lists. Same excerpt is not flagged twice when it also matches `lexicon.avoid`.
- Anth.us seed `rules:` includes Chatticus-quality brochure hedges and intensifiers that belong on an engineering blog (`coming soon`, `we're just getting started`, `revolutionary`, `seamless`, `game-changing`, `transformative`, `cutting-edge`, `unlock`, `leverage`). It does **not** import Chatticus standfirst insider terms (`model`, `API`, `latency`, `repo`) and does **not** turn on `contrastCap` (Anth.us house voice uses “X, not Y”).
- `publications/anthus/editorial-corpus/` (or equivalent) holds:
  - **must-fail** drafts with the expected rule finding (at least the brochure hedges/intensifiers above)
  - **must-pass** excerpts drawn from existing Anth.us reference samples that must produce **no** `rules:` findings
- Behave covers must-fail and must-pass. Adding a must-fail example that is not caught is the specified way to extend a rule.
- `papyrus editorial diagnose` accepts `--text` **or** `--draft` (not both) so an operator can check a candidate sentence without writing a file (Chatticus `--standfirst` isolated check). Draft path remains read-only when `--draft` is used.
- Diagnose remains advisory: JSON on stdout (or `--output`); it does not rewrite; it is not a fail-closed publish gate.
- Detector-score keys stay forbidden.

## Out of scope

- Hosting or migrating chattic.us onto Papyrus.
- Replacing or deleting Chattic.us-web `check_editorial_rules.py` (their site keeps its gate until the CMS revisit).
- Chatticus standfirst insider-term / proper-noun logic.
- Live HTML smoke (`check_live_copy.py`) and pinned-copy test contracts.
- Rewrite options (PPY-73906c), steer CLI (PPY-9edba1), verifier (PPY-5ca22f), Newsroom UI.

## Gherkin

```gherkin
Feature: Data-driven editorial rules for diagnose
  As a publication operator
  I want banned lists and patterns in the style profile
  So brochure-speak is flagged from data, and house-voice excerpts keep passing

  Scenario: Banned intensifiers come from the profile
    Given a style profile whose rules.bannedIntensifiers includes "seamless"
    And a draft that says "a seamless workflow for every team"
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is a finding whose excerpt includes "seamless"

  Scenario: Anth.us does not treat engineering vocabulary as insider terms
    Given the Anth.us style profile
    And a draft that says "Check latency in the repository" and does not use banned intensifiers
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there is no rules finding for "latency" or "repository"

  Scenario: Must-fail brochure copy is caught
    Given a must-fail corpus draft that uses "revolutionary" and "coming soon"
    And the Anth.us style profile
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then findings include those banned terms

  Scenario: Must-pass house-voice excerpts are not flagged by rules
    Given the Anth.us style profile
    And a must-pass excerpt from an Anth.us reference sample
    When I run the diagnose command
    Then there are no findings produced by profile rules

  Scenario: Diagnose a text snippet without a draft file
    Given a loadable style profile
    When I run the diagnose command with --text "This seamless platform will revolutionize workflows" and no --draft
    Then it writes versioned diagnostic JSON
    And the result does not include rewritten prose
```
payload.title: Data-driven editorial rules and two-sided corpus
